extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, hearing examiners, administrative lawyers, and practitioners handling contested cases under Montana MAPA
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing contested-case administrative hearings under the Montana Administrative Procedure Act (MAPA), covering the hearing record, evidence rules, official notice, hearing examiners, disqualification, proposed and final orders, ex parte contacts, license-related hearings, and judicial review/petition filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the record in a contested case
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) The record in a contested case shall include: (a) All pleadings, motions, intermediate rulings. (b) All evidence received or considered, including a stenographic record of oral proceedings when demanded by a party. (c) A statement of matters officially noticed. (d) Questions and offers of proof, objections, and rulings thereon. (e) Proposed findings and exceptions. (f) Any decision, opinion or report by the hearing examiner or agency member presiding at the hearing. (g) All staff memoranda or data submitted to the hearing examiner or members of the agency as evidence in connection with their consideration of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCrory added reference to stenographic records and limited the staff memoranda provision by inserting 'as evidence' to exclude staff legal memoranda prepared for decisionmakers. The record is the sole basis for agency findings of fact and for judicial review; parties must have opportunity to respond to evidence the agency may consider or rely upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription of stenographic record and cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) The stenographic record of oral proceedings or any part thereof shall be transcribed on request of any party. Unless otherwise provided by statute, the cost of the transcription shall be paid by the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must transcribe upon request; ordering who ultimately pays may be subject to court determination but statute places default cost on requesting party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for findings of fact
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) Findings of facts shall be based exclusively on the evidence and on matters officially noticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process requires agency decisionmakers' findings be grounded solely on the hearing record and officially noticed matters; parties must be afforded an opportunity to contest evidence considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of rules of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Except as otherwise provided by statute relating directly to an agency, agencies shall be bound by common law and statutory rules of evidence. Objections to evidentiary offers may be made and shall be noted in the record. When a hearing will be expedited and the interests of the parties will not be prejudiced substantially, any part of the evidence may be received in written form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some statutes exempt certain agency hearings from formal rules; agencies commonly follow evidence rules but may relax them to expedite hearings. Objections must be preserved in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence — copies and comparison rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Documentary evidence may be received in the form of copies or excerpts, if the original is not readily available. Upon request, parties shall be given an opportunity to compare the copy with the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies can accept copies where originals unavailable, but must allow parties to inspect originals on request to preserve cross-examination and challenge rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to cross-examine authors of agency documents
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) A party shall have the right to conduct cross-examinations required for a full and true disclosure of facts, including the right to cross-examine the author of any document prepared by or on behalf of or for the use of the agency and offered in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision was added to ensure documentary evidence offered against a party is subject to cross-examination; preserves confrontation and testing of agency-prepared evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notice — permissible matters and notice to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) Notice may be taken of judicially cognizable facts. In addition, notice may be taken of generally recognized technical or scientific facts within the agency's specialized knowledge. Parties shall be notified either before or during the hearing, or by reference in preliminary reports or otherwise, of the material noticed, including any staff memoranda or data, and they shall be afforded an opportunity to contest the material so noticed. The agency's experience, technical competence, and specialized knowledge may be utilized in the evaluation of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may officially notice facts in their expertise area but must notify parties and allow contest. Commentary notes agencies seldom take official notice in practice while some specialized agencies do routinely rely on industry conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and powers of hearing examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: (1)-(2) An agency shall have authority to appoint hearing examiners for the conduct of hearings in contested cases. Agency members or hearing examiners presiding over hearings shall be authorized to administer oaths or affirmations; issue subpoenas pursuant to section 20 (82-4220) of this act; provide for the taking of testimony by deposition; regulate the course of hearings, including setting the time and place for continued hearings and fixing the time for filing of briefs or other documents; and direct parties to appear and confer to consider simplification of the issues by consent of the parties. All testimony shall be given under oath or affirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing examiners have broad procedural authority to manage hearings. Testimony must be under oath to preserve the integrity of the record for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of hearing examiners and agency members
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) A hearing examiner or agency member may at any time disqualify himself. On the filing in good faith of a timely and sufficient affidavit of personal bias or other disqualification of a hearing examiner or agency member, the agency shall determine the matter as a part of the record and decision in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history shows earlier drafts were more stringent; current version commits disqualification decisions to agency discretion and subjects them to judicial review only as they may taint the final decision. Forms and sample affidavits (Form 12) are referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal for decision (proposed orders) and party rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When in a contested case a majority of the officials of the agency who are to render the final decision have not heard the case or read the record, the decision, if adverse to a party ... may not be made until a proposal for decision is served upon the parties and an opportunity is afforded to each party adversely affected to file exceptions and present briefs and oral argument to the officials who are to render the decision. The proposal for decision shall contain a statement of the reasons therefor and of each issue of fact or law necessary to the proposed decision, prepared by the person who conducted the hearing unless he becomes unavailable to the agency. If the person who conducted the hearing becomes unavailable to the agency, proposed findings of fact may be prepared by a person who has read the record only if the demeanor of witnesses is considered immaterial by all parties. The parties may waive compliance with this section by written stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure decisionmakers master the record and to prevent 'signing on the dotted line.' Amendment history addresses who may draft proposals and preserves parties' right to waive the requirement by stipulation. Attorney General model rules clarify argument rights for parties benefiting from proposed decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and notification requirements for final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A final decision or order adverse to a party in a contested case shall be in writing or stated in the record. A final decision shall include findings of fact and conclusions of law, separately stated. Findings of fact, if set forth in statutory language, shall be accompanied by a concise and explicit statement of the underlying facts supporting the findings. If, in accordance with agency rules, a party submitted proposed findings of fact, the decision shall include a ruling upon each proposed finding. Parties shall be notified either personally or by mail of any decision or order. Upon request, a copy of the decision or order shall be delivered or mailed forthwith to each party and to his attorney of record. Each conclusion of law shall be supported by authority or by a reasoned opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary emphasizes agencies must go beyond conclusory statutory language and state basic/underlying facts to support ultimate findings; courts may allow inferential clarity in some cases. Model rules and forms suggest practical ways to comply (e.g., ruling on proposed findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and effectiveness of agency decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Each agency shall index and make available for public inspection all final decisions and orders, including declaratory rulings under 82-4218. No such agency decision or order is valid or effective against any person or party nor may it be invoked by the agency for any purpose until it has been made available for public inspection as herein required. This provision is not applicable in favor of any person or party who has actual knowledge thereof or when a state statute or federal statute or regulation prohibits public disclosure of the contents of a decision or order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish and index final decisions before enforcing them against persons generally; exceptions exist for confidentiality or when person already has actual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications by decisionmakers after notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless required for disposition of ex parte matters authorized by law, the person or persons who are charged with the duty of rendering a decision or to make findings of fact and conclusions of law in a contested case, after issuance of notice of hearing, shall not communicate with any party or his representative in connection with any issue of fact or law in such case except upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision is limited to after issuance of notice of hearing (not preliminary investigations). Legislature did not further restrict communications with non-parties; parties (and their attorneys) remain constrained by professional ethics rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of MAPA contested-case procedures to licensing actions
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) When the grant, denial, renewal, revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, limitation, transfer, or amendment of a license is required by law to be preceded by notice and opportunity for hearing, the provisions of this part concerning contested cases apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of license is broad and includes many permits/certificates. Agencies must follow contested-case procedures where statute or constitutional right requires hearing; typical initial license denials that fail on face of statutory criteria may be handled without contested-case hearings in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely application for license renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) When a licensee has made timely and sufficient application for the renewal of a license or a new license with reference to any activity of a continuing nature, the existing license does not expire until the application has been finally determined by the agency and, in case the application is denied or the terms of the new license limited, until the last day for seeking review of the agency order or a later date fixed by order of the reviewing court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a timely renewal application tolls expiration of the existing license pending final administrative determination and any review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement before license revocation and emergency summary suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) No revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, or amendment of any license is lawful unless, prior to the institution of agency proceedings, the agency gave notice by mail to the licensee of facts or conduct which warrant the intended action and the licensee was given an opportunity to show compliance with all lawful requirements for the retention of the license. If the agency finds that public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action and incorporates a finding to that effect in its order, summary suspension of a license may be ordered pending proceedings for revocation or other action. These proceedings shall be promptly instituted and determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide pre-proceeding notice and opportunity to respond before license actions, except in narrowly justified emergency circumstances with a written finding and prompt follow-up proceedings. Model rules/forms exist for immediate suspension notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review — exhaustion, scope, and immediate review exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: (1)(a) A person who has exhausted all administrative remedies available within the agency and who is aggrieved by a final decision in a contested case is entitled to judicial review under this part. This section does not limit utilization of or the scope of judicial review available under other means of review, redress, relief, or trial de novo provided by statute. A preliminary, procedural, or intermediate agency action or ruling is immediately reviewable if review of the final agency decision would not provide an adequate remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is required ordinarily; some intermediate or procedural agency actions may be immediately reviewable where final review is inadequate. Statutory alternative review routes are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review — issues preserved and ability to challenge statute validity
rubrics_metrics.description: (1)(b) A party who proceeds before an agency under the terms of a particular statute shall not be precluded from questioning the validity of that statute on judicial review, but such party may not raise any other question not raised before the agency, unless it is shown to the satisfaction of the court that there was good cause for failure to raise the question before the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may challenge statute validity on review even if they proceeded under it, but generally cannot raise issues not presented to the agency without showing good cause; statute ensures agencies have notice of issues to rule upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a petition for review — timing, venue, and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(a)-(b) Proceedings for review shall be instituted by filing a petition in district court within 30 days after service of the final decision of the agency or, if a rehearing is requested, within 30 days after the decision thereon. Except as otherwise provided by statute, the petition shall be filed in the district court for the county where the petitioner resides or has his principal place of business or where the agency maintains its principal office. Copies of the petition shall be promptly served upon the agency and all parties of record. The petition shall include a concise statement of the facts upon which jurisdiction and venue are based, a statement of the manner in which the petitioner is aggrieved, and the ground or grounds specified in subsection (7) of this section upon which the petitioner contends he is entitled to relief. The petition shall demand the relief to which the petitioner believes he is entitled, and the demand for relief may be in the alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets strict 30-day filing period and minimal content requirements for petitions (jurisdiction/venue facts, how aggrieved, grounds). Case law clarifies aspects (e.g., estoppel where agency misleads about MAPA compliance; rehearing requires agency rule permitting it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition does not stay enforcement by default
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Unless otherwise provided by statute, the filing of the petition shall not stay enforcement of the agency's decision. The agency may grant or the reviewing court may order a stay upon terms which it considers proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should seek a stay explicitly from the agency or court; automatic stays exist only where statute provides.
